title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Carbon (C, Z=6) is the interval [12.0096,12.0116]
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Carbon (C, Z=6) as [12.0096,12.0116], with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 6, symbol C, as Carbon. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Carbon as the interval [12.0096,12.0116]. This interval is the set of atomic-weight values NIST assigns to normal materials. It is not the uncertainty of one weighing. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: C-12 relative atomic mass 12.0000000(00), isotopic composition 0.9893(8); C-13 relative atomic mass 13.00335483507(23), isotopic composition 0.0107(8); C-14 relative atomic mass 14.0032419884(40), isotopic composition blank. A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
